ety.text: Borrowed from Classical Persian عدن ('adan), from Arabic عَدْن (ʕadn), from Biblical Hebrew עֵדֶן (ʿḗḏen).

s.g: Aden (a port city, the largest city in Yemen; the former capital of South Yemen)
affliction, adversity, scourge, distress, misfortune, trouble

ety.text: Borrowed from Classical Persian آفت (āfat), from Arabic آفَة (ʔāfa). Compare Bengali আফত (aphot).

s.g: emphatic of इस (is): only this, just this

Borrowed from Classical Persian کمی (kamī). By surface analysis, कम (kam) + -ई (-ī).

ety.text: Borrowed from Classical Persian قَسَم (qasam), from Arabic قَسَم (qasam). Compare Bengali কসম (qôsom), Punjabi ਕ਼ਸਮ (qasam).

s.g: Jammu (a city in India, winter capital of the union territory of Jammu and Kashmir)
Jammu (the southern region of the union territory of Jammu and Kashmir)

ety.text: From Sanskrit जम्बू (jambū). Traditionally considered to be named after Jambu Lochan.

s.g: shed, hut, usually built of earth or clay
x: जिन टिकौनों से उसने अपने मन को सँभाला था, वे सब इस भूकंप में नीचे आ रहे और वह झोंपड़ा नीचे गिर पड़ा।

ety.text: From a variant of Prakrit झुंपडा f (jhuṃpaḍā) from *झुप्प (jhuppa, “hut”) + Middle Indo-Aryan -𑀟- (-ḍa-) + -𑀓- (-ka-) of uncertain substrate origin. Compare Nepali झोप्रो (jhopro), Gujarati ઝૂંપડું (jhū̃pḍũ), Assamese জুপুৰি (zupuri), Marathi झोपडी (jhopḍī).

Inherited from Proto-New Indo-Aryan *डब्ब (ḍabba) of unknown substrate origin. Doublet of डब्बा (ḍabbā). Compare Marathi डाव (ḍāv, “hollowed coconut”), Bengali ডাব (ḍabo), Odia ଡାବ (ḍāba, “raw coconut”). Also compare Swahili dafu, an Indo-Aryan borrowing.
From ताड़ (tāṛ, “palmyra, toddy palm”) + -ई (-ī), ultimately from Dravidian.
Learned borrowing from Sanskrit नवनीत (navanīta). Doublet of नोनी (nonī) and नवनी (navnī).

s.g: a male given name, Navneet, from Sanskrit

ety.text: Learned borrowing from Sanskrit नवनीत (navanīta). Doublet of नोनी (nonī) and नवनी (navnī).

s.g: Exodus (the second of the Books of Moses in the Old Testament of the Bible, the second book in the Torah describing the Exodus)
Exodus (the departure of the Hebrew slaves from Egypt under the leadership of Moses)

ety.text: Learned borrowing from Sanskrit निर्गमन (nirgamana). Proper noun sense is a semantic loan from Ancient Greek Ἔξοδος (Éxodos).

s.g: refers to the second of the five critical stages (joints or sandhis) that structure the plot of a play, in ancient Indian natyashastra
a female given name, Prarthana, from Sanskrit

ety.text: From फूलना (phūlnā, “to swell, to puff”). Cognate with Sindhi फुल्को m sg (fulko, “roti”).
Inherited from Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀩𑀻𑀟𑀕 (bīḍaga), from Sanskrit वीटक (vīṭaka). Cognate with Marathi विडा (viḍā).

Ezekiel (a book of the Old Testament of the Bible)

ety.text: Learned borrowing from Biblical Hebrew יְחֶזְקֵאל (y'ḥez'qel, “God strengthens”).
Borrowed from Sanskrit समानुभूति (samānubhūti). By surface analysis, सम (sam, “same”) + अनुभूति (anubhūti, “feeling”).

s.g: comrade (fellow communist or other political leftist)

ety.text: Inherited from Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀲𑀢𑁆𑀣𑀺𑀅 (satthia), from Sanskrit सार्थिक (sārthika), from सार्थ (sārtha) + -इक (-ika). Compare Nepali साथी (sāthī), Marathi साथी (sāthī), and Sindhi ساٿِي (sāthī). Synchronically analyzable as साथ (sāth) + -ई (-ī).

s.g: one who knows the ways of सुलफ़ा smoking and dealing

ety.text: Learned borrowing from Sanskrit हं॒स (haṃsá). Doublet of हाँस (hā̃s).
